findings.summary: Forked copy of upstream `lheading` instead of the wrap-and-delegate pattern used for `list`
findings.evidence: `lheadingRule` reproduces ~60 lines of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` verbatim (terminator loop, token pushes, `asciiTrim` re-implementation at lines 17-23) with one added guard, while the sibling `list` change (lines 178-195) delegates to the stock rule via `getRuleFn`. The forked copy silently drifts on every markdown-it upgrade (and duplicates markdown-it's private `asciiTrim`), whereas the same one-line guard could be expressed as a wrapper around the original rule. Approach/consistency preference, not a correctness claim.

findings.summary: Depends on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry to fetch the stock `list` rule
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: Array<{name, fn, enabled}> }` and reads an undocumented internal. This ties a notes-scoped plugin to markdown-it internals (a layering/robustness fit issue); capturing the rule via a supported mechanism, or registering a separate paragraph-terminator rule before `paragraph` (the pattern already used by `details-plugin.ts:104`), would keep the plugin on public API.

findings.summary: Deviation is broader than the issue: empty bullets now interrupt any paragraph, and a lone top-level `-` underline is disabled globally
findings.evidence: The issue (#517) is specifically about an empty *nested* bullet under a list item. The implementation applies globally: `lheadingRule` rejects any single-dash setext underline (so `Heading\n-` at top level no longer produces an `<h2>`), and `wrappedList` lets an empty bullet terminate *any* paragraph (`foo\n- ` now starts a list). This is documented as a deliberate deviation in docs/design/notes/notes.md:276-299, so it is a scope judgement rather than an unmet criterion, but it is more surface than the issue asked for and the doc does not call out the top-level single-dash-heading regression explicitly.

findings.summary: Design-doc note omits the user-visible side effect it introduces (single-dash setext headings stop working)
findings.evidence: The added section says "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render" but does not state that the previously-valid single-dash setext underline (`Heading\n-`) is now permanently unavailable in notes. Recording that trade-off is what keeps the canonical subsystem doc honest about the deviation.

findings.summary: `wrappedList` short-circuits before the stock list rule's indent/listIndent guards, so paragraphs can be split where upstream would keep a lazy continuation
findings.evidence: The early `return true` (lines 182-191) runs before `originalList`, bypassing every precondition the upstream `list` rule checks in silent mode — notably the deep-nesting special case `if (state.listIndent >= 0 && state.sCount[startLine] - state.listIndent >= 4 && state.sCount[startLine] < state.blkIndent) return false`. For such a line (an over-indented lone `-` inside deeply nested lists) upstream returns false and the line stays a lazy paragraph continuation; here the paragraph is terminated, yet the subsequent non-silent `list` call still returns false via that same guard, so the `-` ends up as a separate paragraph instead of continuation text. `isEmptyBulletLine` should re-use the same indent guards (or delegate to `originalList` first and only override the empty-item rejection).

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__`; a shape change throws at module import and takes down the whole notes preview
findings.evidence: `ruler.__rules__.find(...)` plus `throw new Error(...)` on line 212 runs at import time via `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` (preview.ts:48), which is executed at module scope. Since `markdown-it` is depended on as `^14.1.0`, any minor release that renames/reshapes the private registry turns a rendering degradation into an uncaught module-evaluation error that breaks the entire notes view, not just empty bullets. A safer fallback (e.g. no-op wrapper when the rule can't be found) would fail soft.

findings.summary: Reimplemented heading-content trim diverges from upstream `String.prototype.trim()`
findings.evidence: Upstream `rules_block/lheading` trims the heading content with `.trim()`, which also strips Unicode whitespace (e.g. U+00A0, U+2028). `asciiTrim` (lines 19-23) strips only the six ASCII whitespace codes, so a heading such as `Heading \n===` will keep the trailing non-breaking space in the rendered `<h1>`, unlike stock markdown-it. Harmless but an unintended behavior delta in a rule advertised as a mirror of upstream.

findings.summary: Restoring `state.parentType` on the no-underline path diverges from upstream lheading
findings.evidence: Lines 129-132 restore `state.parentType = oldParentType` before `return false`; upstream markdown-it's lheading returns false while leaving `parentType` set to `'paragraph'`. This is arguably more correct, but it is an unannounced behavioral deviation from the rule this file claims to mirror, and any downstream rule that (accidentally) depended on the leaked `'paragraph'` parent type will now see a different value.

findings.summary: The `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` chain restoration the code calls out as a hazard is untested
findings.evidence: The plugin re-registers `list` via `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: [...] })` and its own comment warns that getting this wrong makes `list` stop terminating paragraphs/references/blockquotes (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:203-211). No added test renders a list inside or after a blockquote (`> - 1\n>   -`), a list following a link-reference definition, or a plain non-empty list interrupting a paragraph (`text\n- item`). If the alt array were dropped or mistyped, all added tests would still pass since they all start at the top of the document with a list.
searchedFor: grep for '>' blockquote fixtures and '[ref]:' in packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts

findings.summary: No test pins the top-level behavior change `Heading\n-` (used to be an h2, now a paragraph plus empty list)
findings.evidence:
The lone-dash guard (`isLoneDash`, list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:118) applies at any indent, so top-level `Text
-` no longer renders as `<h2>` — a user-visible deviation from CommonMark for ordinary prose, not just nested list items. The added tests only cover the nested `- 1
  -` shape; nothing asserts what top-level `Text
-` now produces, so the scope of the deviation is unpinned by tests.
searchedFor: grep for setext fixtures in packages/notes/src

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` regex has quadratic (ReDoS-style) worst case on attacker-supplied note content, replacing upstream's linear `String.prototype.trim()`
findings.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is applied at line 134 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)`, i.e. the full paragraph text preceding a setext underline. The second alternative `[ws]+$` is unanchored: for an interior whitespace run of length n that is NOT at end-of-string (e.g. `"A" + " ".repeat(200000) + "B\n==="`), the backtracking engine restarts the greedy run at every offset inside the run and fails `$` each time — O(n^2) steps (~5e9 for n=1e5), freezing the rendering thread. Upstream markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses `.getLines(...).trim()`, which is linear; this fork introduces the quadratic path. Attack chain: a workspace collaborator saves such a line into a shared note (content is Yorkie-synced), `editor.ts:150 renderPreview()` calls `preview.render(currentDoc())` on every doc update in every viewer's browser, and `preview.ts:165 md.render(markdown)` hangs the tab — a persistent, stored client-side DoS for all collaborators (no note-size cap exists in packages/notes). I could not execute the regex to time it, hence medium confidence; the quadratic structure itself is evident from the pattern.

findings.summary: Vendored fork of markdown-it's `lheading` rule will not receive upstream security fixes (parser hardening / ReDoS patches) on dependency upgrade
findings.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (line 175) permanently swaps out the upstream rule for a copy of markdown-it 14.x's implementation pasted at lines 70-155. Any future markdown-it patch release that hardens `lheading` (markdown-it has historically shipped parser DoS fixes in block rules) will be installed by `pnpm audit`/dependency bumps but silently NOT applied to the notes preview, because this fork shadows it. There is no version pin or assertion tying the fork to the upstream version it was copied from, so the divergence is invisible at upgrade time. Impact if real: an unpatched parser rule running on collaborator-controlled content.

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` depends on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws at module-import time if it ever disappears, hard-failing the notes preview
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: ... }` (line 208-210) and throws `new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')` (line 212) when the private field is renamed/reshaped. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is invoked at module scope in `preview.ts:48` (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`), so the throw happens during ESM evaluation of `preview.ts` — uncatchable by any caller, taking down the whole notes editor module rather than degrading to stock markdown behaviour. A routine security upgrade of markdown-it therefore risks availability loss of the notes feature. Reported as a hardening/availability concern: prefer a defensive fallback (skip the wrapper, keep stock `list`) over a module-init throw.

findings.summary: The `lheading` replacement is global to the preview renderer, so a valid single-dash setext heading anywhere (including top level, outside any list) now renders as a paragraph plus an empty bullet — a rendering change to already-stored user notes
findings.evidence:
The guard `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105) is not scoped to nested/list context, and `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (line 175) replaces the rule for the single shared renderer used by every note (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:14,48; consumed by packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:117). Existing content such as `Title\n-` previously rendered `

Title

` and now renders body text followed by an empty `
`. docs/design/notes/notes.md:297 only promises that `---` and `=` underlines are untouched, so the top-level single-dash case is an undocumented, untested consequence for pre-existing documents.

findings.summary: `lheading` is replaced wholesale rather than delegated, and the `list` wrapper captures whatever `list` fn exists at `md.use` time — both silently depend on the plugin ordering in `preview.ts`
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 overwrites `lheading` with a frozen copy of markdown-it 14.x's rule, discarding any `lheading` customisation installed by an earlier plugin (`md.use(taskLists)` / `md.use(katexPlugin)` / `md.use(detailsPlugin)` at packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:36,39,44) and any upstream fix shipped inside the `^14.1.0` range. Conversely, `getRuleFn(md,'list')` (line 176) snapshots the `list` rule, so any plugin added *after* packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48 that calls `ruler.at('list', ...)` would silently drop the #517 fix with no test failure. The invariant 'listEmptyBulletPlugin must be the last block-rule plugin' is load-bearing but unenforced and undocumented in preview.ts.

findings.summary: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` passes no options, so markdown-it's `Ruler.at` resets that rule's `alt` chain to `[]`
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 omits the third argument, while the sibling call for `list` at line 197 deliberately restores `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` (the lesson recorded in docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:17-20). In markdown-it 14 the stock `lheading` entry appears to carry no `alt`, so this is likely harmless — but node_modules is not present in this worktree, so I could not confirm against `parser_block.mjs`. If upstream does register `lheading` with an `alt` chain, this line removes it for every rule that consults `getRules(...)`. Confirming needs a read of markdown-it 14.x `lib/parser_block.mjs` `_rules`.
searchedFor: grep alt: in markdown-it parser_block (module not installed)

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present as described (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105,107 — `isLoneDash` is not scoped by `state.blkIndent`), and top-level `Text\n-` does fall through to the wrappedList terminator (lines 181-193). But this is the explicitly specified behavior, not a logic error: docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299 states that "a **lone single `-`** (the empty-bullet shape) is never a setext underline, and an empty bullet is allowed to interrupt a paragraph so it nests as an empty child item", and that only "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched" — i.e. the doc knowingly gives up single-dash setext H2 document-wide. What remains is (a) a design-scope objection (should have been limited to blkIndent > 0) owned by the design/architecture lens, (b) a slightly overstated doc comment at lines 64-65 (nit), and (c) a test-coverage gap at preview.test.ts:182, which is test quality and expressly outside the correctness lane. samples.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` regex has quadratic (ReDoS-style) worst case on attacker-supplied note content, replacing upstream's linear `String.prototype.trim()`

The second alternative `[ws]+$` is unanchored: for an interior whitespace run of length n that is NOT at end-of-string (e.g. `"A" + " ".repeat(200000) + "B\n==="`), the backtracking engine restarts the greedy run at every offset inside the run and fails `$` each time — O(n^2) steps (~5e9 for n=1e5), freezing the rendering thread. Upstream markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses `.getLines(...).trim()`, which is linear; this fork introduces the quadratic path. I could not execute the regex to time it, hence medium confidence; the quadratic structure itself is evident from the pattern.

verdict.reason:
The reviewer's literal facts check out — `getRuleFn` does read `md.block.ruler.__rules__` and throws when the entry is missing (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:207-214), it is invoked at module scope via `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48), and `editor.ts` imports `NotePreview` at top level (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20) with `markdown-it: ^14.1.0` declared (packages/notes/package.json:63). But nothing in this repository is actually broken by it, and the claimed breakage is not a blast-radius defect under this lens's rubric.

(1) No reachable failure path exists today. The workspace pins markdown-it to 14.3.0 (pnpm-lock.yaml:7083, 16046), where `Ruler.__rules__` and the `list` block rule both exist. I grepped every place the notes package touches the block ruler (details-plugin.ts:104, list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:71/175/197/208) — no plugin in the pipeline (task-lists, katex, detailsPlugin) removes or renames the `list` rule, so the `if (!rule) throw` branch is dead with the resolved dependency. The plugin is exercised end-to-end by the existing preview tests (packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:151-192), which render through this exact module-init path.

(2) What remains is a hypothetical: "some future markdown-it release inside ^14 might hide `__rules__`". That is dependency-fragility / private-API-coupling — a robustness and design concern, not "a caller left broken by a changed contract", "a guard with a reachable bypass", or "a violated invariant another module depends on". No out-of-diff consumer relies on an old contract here: `NotePreview`'s exported shape, `render()` signature, and preview.ts's module-init side-effect model are unchanged for editor.ts:20 and preview.test.ts:2 (the only two importers; the third hit is archived docs). The trigger condition and the throw both live entirely inside the diff, which the lens explicitly defers to the correctness/design lenses.

I am refuting the blocking claim, not the observation: replacing the private-registry read with a non-fatal lookup is a reasonable hardening, but it does not gate this merge under the blast-radius rubric.
